references.context: Module theory: isomorphism class of an R-module M under invertible R-linear homomorphisms, the equivalence class of all R-modules isomorphic to M; this source restricts representatives to finitely generated R-modules.
references.reason: Module-isomorphism equivalence classes are reusable beyond this particular K-theory group and are not ordinary bijections of underlying sets.
references.matching_note: Distinguish module isomorphism from graph or ring isomorphism; compare later with the finite projective class occurrence.

references.context: Abelian-group theory: abelian group presented by generators and relations, constructed as the free abelian group on the generator set modulo the subgroup generated by specified formal relations. Here a relation [M]-[M′]-[M″]=0 arises from a short exact module sequence.
references.reason: Presenting an abelian group by generators and additive relations is an independently reusable construction; the exact-sequence relations are source-specific.
references.matching_note: Contrast additive K′_0 exact-sequence relations with split/direct-sum K_0 relations; do not equate the two K-groups.

references.phrase: isomorphism class of finite projective module
references.context: Module theory: isomorphism class of a finitely generated projective R-module under invertible R-linear homomorphisms, as a restricted instance of the general module-isomorphism equivalence relation.
references.reason: This group is built on module-isomorphism classes, not on a chosen representative or merely a bijection of underlying sets.
references.matching_note: Compare to the more general finite-module isomorphism-class prerequisite in global reviewed alias work.

references.phrase: abelian group presentation by direct sums
references.context: Algebraic K-theory: group completion of the commutative monoid of isomorphism classes of finitely generated projective R-modules under direct sum, imposing [P⊕Q]=[P]+[Q] (equivalently split exact relations).
references.reason: Commutative-monoid group completion is reusable and differs from the exact-sequence relations of K′_0 on all finite modules.
references.matching_note: Preserve split exactness, direct sum and finite projectivity; no automatic identification with Grothendieck K′_0 of all finitely generated modules.

references.disposition: For projective quotient modules the short exact sequence splits; relation here is direct-sum additivity.

references.context: Commutative algebra: degree-n associated-graded module component m^nM/m^{n+1}M of the maximal-ideal filtration of a finite module M over a local ring (R,m), formed as a quotient module with induced residue-ring action.
references.reason: The associated graded components and filtration quotients are reusable beyond the Hilbert polynomial and are not the same as the cumulative M/m^{n+1}M.
references.matching_note: Review general quotient-module candidate equivalence and the difference between the Hilbert function of graded pieces and Hilbert-Samuel cumulative length.

references.context: Algebra: polynomial P(T) in the univariate polynomial algebra ℚ[T], evaluated at sufficiently large nonnegative integer n, with rational coefficients and finite degree.
references.reason: A polynomial over the rational coefficient field is a reusable algebraic object distinct from the eventual-equality condition that defines this Hilbert polynomial.
references.matching_note: Compare with existing general unital-coefficient polynomial algebra candidate; rational coefficients specialize that construction.

references.disposition: This is eventual equality; no assertion is made for small n or that it equals a cumulative Hilbert–Samuel function.

references.matching_note: Source occurrence 'injective ring map i:D to F' expresses ordinary injectivity of the underlying map; distinguish universal injectivity/pure module maps and categorical coproduct structure arrows.

references.context: Integer arithmetic: binary addition on integers constructed from natural-number difference classes, inducing [(a,b)]+[(c,d)]=[(a+c,b+d)] and requiring independence from representatives; it gives an abelian group with zero and additive inverses.
references.reason: The integer addition operation is reusable in arithmetic and its quotient-class well-definedness is not certified by the existing integer-set definition alone.
references.matching_note: Operation prerequisite, with theorem-level well-definedness and algebraic laws deferred to the global audit.

references.context: Integer arithmetic: product on natural-number difference classes given by [(a,b)]·[(c,d)]=[(ac+bd,ad+bc)], requiring well-definedness on equivalence classes and yielding a distributive unital ring operation.
references.reason: The multiplication of integers is a reusable mathematical operation; the underlying integer set and abstract ring axioms do not by themselves establish the concrete operation.
references.matching_note: Preserve integer quotient construction and flag representative independence and ring axioms for separate mathematical proof audit.

references.disposition: Ring Z has its usual unital commutative structure and not all nonzero elements have multiplicative inverses.
